prompt: An ultra-wide retro arcade credits end card, SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, subtle CRT scanline glow; the final quiet frame after the credits roll. The scene is a pale dawn over the curved rim of a distant planet: thin rose-pink cloud bars over a cream-gold horizon band along the bottom, a half-sun just clearing the planet rim, and above it the sky rising through soft lilac into a lifted deep navy at the very top, never pure black, with the last few stars fading. In the lower left third, a single small steel-blue dart-shaped fighter with a cyan canopy flies level and unhurried toward the left edge of the frame, a relaxed warm orange engine glow and a thin straight contrail behind it. The middle and upper middle are calm open sky, and there, centered and perfectly straight-on, the game's title "SHMUP CUP" in huge heavy chunky block capital letters filled with a vertical gradient from pale yellow through orange into red, each letter with a thick dark navy outline, a soft navy drop shadow and a single white highlight along its top edge. Directly below the title, centered in smaller straight-on capital letters of pale ivory with thin navy outlines, the single line "THANK YOU FOR PLAYING". Warm, plain-spoken and complete, like the last page of a picture book. The only text in the image is "SHMUP CUP" and "THANK YOU FOR PLAYING": no credits list, no dates, no numbers, no other words, watermark or signature anywhere.
